name: Huckleberry Cake
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: soda dissolved in hot water
ingredients.originalText: 1 teaspoonful soda dissolved in hot water

ingredients.name: ripe, fresh huckleberries, thickly dredged with flour
ingredients.originalText: 1 qt. ripe, fresh huckleberries, thickly dredged with flour

instructions.text: Stir the butter and sugar to a cream
Add the milk, the flour, and spice
Add the whites whipped stiff and the soda
At the last stir in the huckleberries with a wooden spoon or paddle, not to bruise them
Bake in a loaf or card, in a moderate but steady oven, until a straw comes out clean from the thickest part

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stir the butter and sugar to a cream
2. Add the beaten yolks
3. Add the milk, the flour, and spice
4. Add the whites whipped stiff and the soda
5. At the last stir in the huckleberries with a wooden spoon or paddle, not to bruise them
6. Bake in a loaf or card, in a moderate but steady oven, until a straw comes out clean from the thickest part
